stem.en: A source of sound in air vibrates faster, so the frequency of its sound increases. What happens?

text.en: Fewer compressions pass a fixed place each second.
More compressions pass a fixed place each second.
The sound travels faster through the air.

explanation.en: Frequency is the number of oscillations each second at a fixed place. A higher frequency means more compressions pass each second. The speed in air stays the same, so the wavelength gets shorter.

hints.en: In the same air, does the speed change?
